title: Implementing HUMAN Skills Studio Framework, Phase 3
author: Doan Winkel
summary: This is the third installment of Winkel’s phased guide to implementing the HUMAN Skills Studio Framework, which uses generative AI in college courses to develop human skills. Phase 3 (months 8 to 10) argues that the framework must become the course operating system rather than an add-on, because partial implementation leaves students code-switching and the portfolio feeling like compliance. He expands the portfolio to five to seven episodes capped by a Growth Narrative, and makes AI roles routine classroom vocabulary with increasing student choice. Two authentic human performances worth at least 40 percent of the grade are meant to make gaming the AI-assisted components mathematically insufficient. External feedback from calibrated peers, near-peers, professionals and formal self-assessment adds validity. He closes with anti-gaming design principles, an evidence plan, a workload estimate of about 39 to 47 hours, and a milestone checklist.
points: Full integration is the point: when every assignment uses AI roles and produces portfolio evidence, students internalize the framework rather than performing compliance.
The Growth Narrative is the portfolio’s capstone because the reflective synthesis, not the artifacts, produces the learning.
Weighting two live human performances at 40 percent or more makes success impossible through AI-assisted work alone.
Design against gaming by asking how students transformed AI output and by running unpredictable process probes, rather than trying to prove AI use.
Phase 3 is costed honestly, with tiered review, a minimum viable version and explicit fixes for anxiety, generic peer feedback and unsustainable workload.
quotes: Partial implementation creates confusion. When some assignments use the framework and others don’t, students code-switch rather than internalize. When the portfolio feels separate from graded work, it becomes compliance rather than documentation.

Full integration solves these problems by making the framework unavoidable. Every assignment uses AI roles. Every assignment produces portfolio evidence. Multiple perspectives validate human skill development.

The Growth Narrative is the portfolio’s most important component. It requires students to synthesize across episodes, identify patterns, and articulate learning. This metacognitive demand is what transforms documentation into development.
Phase 3 increases student autonomy in role selection. Where earlier phases prescribed roles, now students choose—and justify.

Authentic assessment means tasks that mirror real-world application—not artificial exercises designed only for grading. Research defines authentic assessment as requiring students to use the same competencies (combinations of knowledge, skills, and attitudes) that they would apply in real professional or civic contexts.

Forget about whether students used AI or not. Instead, ask “How did you transform AI output?” The transformation question is harder to game because it requires articulating intellectual work that either happened or didn’t.
The unpredictability is key. If students know when verification comes, they prepare for those moments. If verification could happen any time, the incentive shifts toward genuine engagement.
